title: [MODEL] Post-reset: consolidate the ML registry and audit the ML development process: per decision slot (D1-D10) keep or retire every model, fold every kept model into the iteration loop with a named competition, and decide one-live vs ensemble/consensus per slot with evidence
note: Operator 2026-11-09 ~18:50Z (chat, paraphrased): after the reset, in the planning session, consolidate the registry and go over the models: what is worth keeping and what is not; retire what is not (it takes space and resources); integrate everything kept into the ML iterative process. More than one ML per decision class is fine, but for each we must know what it is, what it competes on, which one is live, and if more than one is live, why more than one beats one (e.g. consensus votes). A deeper dive into the ML development infrastructure, to confirm we are structured to make progress in the right direction. SCOPE (proposed by manager, for the Thursday plan): (1) inventory from the consolidated feed (ML-REGISTRY-CONSOLIDATE lane, 2026-11-09) by slot -> breed -> lineage; (2) keep/retire per model against a stated rule (beats its slot baseline net of cost on a registered population, or is a live/shadow consumer, or an open unit depends on it); retire = retirement record + artifact/registry cleanup (trainer disk/compute); (3) per slot: champion, challengers and the metric they compete on, demotion signal, and whether live is single or ensemble/consensus, which needs its own pre-registered test vs the single best; (4) process audit: is every kept model in a programme iteration unit (programme-review loop), are slot baselines declared, is family diversity healthy (ml_plan_status.py --diversity), are compute and the queue spent on the slots with the most money at stake. Folds/relates: ML-REGISTRY-LADDER-GAPS, ML-HYGIENE, UI-CATALOG-STRATEGIES-ML, docs/plans/ML-ROADMAP-MECE-2026-11.md section 8.
